original_value: The identification of communities, or modules, is a common operation in the analysis of large biological networks. The Disease Module Identification DREAM challenge established a framework to evaluate clustering approaches in a biomedical context, by testing the association of communities with GWAS-derived common trait and disease genes. We implemented here several extensions of the MolTi software that detects communities by optimizing multiplex (and monoplex) network modularity. In particular, MolTi now runs a randomized version of the Louvain algorithm, can consider edge and layer weights, and performs recursive clustering.  On simulated networks, the randomization procedure clearly improves the detection of communities. On the DREAM challenge benchmark, the results strongly depend on the selected GWAS dataset and enrichment p-value threshold. However, the randomization procedure, as well as the consideration of weighted edges and layers generally increases the number of trait and disease community detected.  The new version of MolTi and the scripts used for the DMI DREAM challenge are available at: https://github.com/gilles-didier/MolTi-DREAM.

result.paraphrase: Identifying communities, or modules, is a routine task in the analysis of large biological networks. The Disease Module Identification DREAM challenge established a biomedical framework for assessing clustering methods by evaluating how communities associate with common trait and disease genes derived from GWAS. Here, we implemented several extensions to MolTi, a program that detects communities by optimizing modularity in multiplex and monoplex networks. MolTi now uses a randomized version of the Louvain algorithm, supports edge and layer weights, and applies recursive clustering. In simulated networks, randomization clearly improves community detection. In the DREAM challenge benchmark, results vary strongly with the chosen GWAS dataset and enrichment p-value threshold. Even so, randomization, along with weighted edges and layers, generally increases the number of detected trait and disease communities. The updated MolTi version and the scripts used for the DMI DREAM challenge are available at: https://github.com/gilles-didier/MolTi-DREAM.
